cohort: 80 females aged 18-45 years, with gestational age above 32 weeks and BMI ≤ 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective cesarean section under general anesthesia.
finding: Intravenous Nalbuphine was more effective than IV Ibuprofen for postoperative pain relief following cesarean section, providing superior pain control, reducing the need for rescue analgesia, and resulting in higher patient satisfaction, though with increased drowsiness.
